claim: The change leaves Chroma's in-process client cache alone: no SQL Lens code reads or changes `SharedSystemClient._identifier_to_system`, so the server log can still show the `AttributeError` on every other failed open. The change does not edit `src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py`. The change leaves memory failures that happen after the store opened, for example an embedding-model download failure during a search, handled as they are today. A call made while the store cannot be opened still runs the whole agent turn, including its model requests, before it returns the error. A message the default workflow handler answers without calling the model (for example `help`) makes no store open attempt; it returns the memory-unavailable error exactly when a failure from an earlier open attempt is recorded.
